checks.name: a3-one-accepted-set-one-predicate-exact-membership
checks.summary: AcceptedRecordSchemas (store.go:62 after the change) is an ordered, closed, duplicate-free declaration and RecordSchemaAccepted (store.go:69) is the single read-side envelope decision; all five read sites call it (store.go:221, 315, 1372, 1490, 1629 after the change). checks.name: a4-all-five-read-sites-behaviourally-proven
checks.summary: With AcceptedRecordSchemas substituted IN THE TEST ONLY to two members {"v1", "v2-expand-probe"} and restored with defer (the internal/scheduler/priority.go scoreFn technique), a document written under the second id is read successfully by every one of the five sites, and a document under a third id "v3-refused-probe" -- deliberately NOT a member of the substituted set -- is refused with ErrInvalidSchema by every one of the five. The concrete store operation per site: (1) store.go:79 DecodeRecord, called directly on the flat JSON codec envelope; (2) store.go:173 decodeDocument, reached through unit.Requirement inside Store.Transact; (3) store.go:1230 the outbox scan, reached through unit.Outboxes inside Store.Transact; (4) store.go:1348 the bounded collection scan in unit.query, reached through unit.Requirements inside Store.Transact; (5) store.go:1484 the bounded collection scan in readCollection, reached through Store.Events. Each case writes a raw document built by encodeDocument and then overrides only the envelope id, so the envelope is the single difference from a native document, and each case runs against its own freshly-named empty installation so no scan assertion is polluted by another case's document. The production set is never widened: the substitution helper fails the test if AcceptedRecordSchemas does not have exactly one member before substituting. verdict: PASS, 15 subtests (5 sites x accepts-second / accepts-native / refuses-third), zero SKIP.

checks.name: a5-written-value-pinned-so-a-bump-announces-itself
checks.summary: TestPinsTheWrittenRecordEnvelopeValueSoABumpCannotRideAlong states in its name what it pins. It asserts: RecordSchema equals the literal "v1" written in the test body; AcceptedRecordSchemas contains RecordSchema; the shipped set has exactly one member and it is that value; every member matches the declared id shape ^v[0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$; the set is duplicate-free; encodeDocument writes that member; and every member of the accepted set round-trips through EncodeRecord/DecodeRecord and through the document encode path, so a store cannot write a value it would refuse to read. The written value and the accepted set are separate declarations (store.go:31 and store.go:62), which is the structural half of the guarantee; the literal pin is the half CI enforces. verdict: PASS.

checks.name: a6-payload-interpretability-for-non-native-ids-only
checks.summary: Under the same test-only two-member substitution, a document carrying the non-native accepted id is refused with ErrInvalidSchema when its payload does not satisfy domain.Validate for its kind, and accepted when it does. The three uninterpretable inputs, asserted at each of the three sites whose kind the domain declares a predicate for (store.go:79 DecodeRecord, store.go:173 decodeDocument via unit.Requirement, store.go:1348 the bounded scan via unit.Requirements): an empty requirement id; the unknown requirement status "not-a-status"; and a payload that is valid JSON of the wrong shape ({"unexpected":"field"}), which decodes into a zero-valued struct and would otherwise look like a legitimate record. Each of the three is additionally asserted to be UNAFFECTED under the native envelope, i.e. today's read path returns exactly what it returns today. NATIVE PATH UNCHANGED, asserted explicitly: validateRecordPayload is a package-level variable holding domain.Validate, a test substitutes a counting wrapper, drives all five read sites with native documents only (DecodeRecord, unit.Requirement, unit.Requirements, unit.Outboxes, Store.Events, Store.Outbox) and asserts the count is ZERO; a positive control on the same counter then observes exactly one call on a non-native read, so the zero is a measured zero and not a dead probe. Measured limit, recorded rather than presented as coverage: domain.Validate describes only Requirement, Increment, Execution and Lease, so at store.go:1230 (kind outbox) and store.go:1484 (kinds event and outbox) the gate is present and reached but has no applicable predicate. Production exposure of the gate is ZERO today because there are no non-native ids; it is exercised only through the test-only substitution. verdict: PASS.
